$comment: The iPhone 6.9-inch listing set: nine frames, in the order App Store Connect takes them.
This file is the ONE source for three things a render needs, which is why it is data
rather than a table copied into the HTML: the caption each frame carries, the app
capture that fills its slot, and the harness state that capture was taken from.
`design/preview/capture.mjs --target frames` reads it to render the committed PNGs,
and `design/store-screenshots/capture-frames.mjs` reads it to re-take the app captures
they are made of. Captions are the plan's (`docs/publishing/listing-screenshots.md`,
'The set — nine shots, claim-first order'); changing one is a re-render, not an edit
Paths are relative to this directory. `cell` and `scenario` are the mock relay's own
that cell with that world pinned, so the frame is the app rendering a real relay
answer and nothing in it is composited.

frames.headline: Every session on your machine, in your pocket.
frames.shows: A running session: turns, tool rows, the tasks and subagents strips, and the composer.

frames.headline: Diffs and code blocks, as your agent writes them.
frames.shows: A real fenced diff, a fenced code block and two tables, with the rows that own the copy control.

frames.headline: Approve each command, before it runs.
frames.shows: The approval card for a destructive command: Approve, Deny, and the always-allow switch.

frames.headline: Every turn, marked as it finishes.
frames.shows: The per-turn checkpoint rail down the transcript's edge: user dashes and completed ticks.

frames.headline: Find any message in the conversation.
frames.shows: The in-conversation find sheet on a query, with its matches and the scope line.

frames.headline: Every computer's sessions, in one list.
frames.shows: The sessions list with another computer's sessions appended to this one's.

frames.headline: Move a session between your computers.
frames.shows: A move's receipt: the phase transcript from prepared to done, and the read it points at.

frames.headline: Ask your agent — it runs on your computer.
frames.shows: The home composer, idle: the first thing a new install shows.

frames.headline: Connect to your own computer.
frames.shows: Sign-in, in its real sparse state: the browser finishes the sign-in, so the app never sees the password.
